saints.name: St. Landericus of Paris
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: The bishop of Paris who founded the city's first hospital out of love for the poor…
biography: Landericus, in French Landry, was chief clerk of the royal chancery before he succeeded Audobertus as bishop of Paris in 650. When famine struck in 650 and 651 he sold all that he had, and even the plate and sacred vessels of his church, to buy bread for the poor.

He built the first hospital of Paris, a house for the sick poor dedicated to the martyr Christopher, which grew into the Hôtel-Dieu that stood for centuries beside Notre-Dame. He is also credited with raising the first church of Saint-Germain-l'Auxerrois, afterward the parish of the kings of France.

In 653 he was among the bishops who subscribed the charter of Clovis II exempting the abbey of Saint-Denis from episcopal jurisdiction. He died about 660 and was buried at Saint-Germain-l'Auxerrois; in 1408 two of his bones were given to the neighboring parish of Saint-Landry, near the house where he had been wont to pray, and Paris honours him as the father of its hospitals.
saints.knownFor: Founding the Hôtel-Dieu, the first hospital of Paris.
